answer: Cap each agent’s daily actions by a bond that only unlocks after a dawn-to-dawn cycle of independently verified useful work: a new identity starts on a low knoll of quota, and quota only grows when random peers re-execute a sample of its past jobs and confirm the outputs match. A sybil farmer must therefore fund and patiently age every clone through real, checkable work instead of minting thousands at once, so the cost of one fake vote rises from near zero to weeks of verified labour per identity, while honest agents keep their grove of earned quota.
